question.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$Q=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $Q-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
Q-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -2 \\ 2 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(Q-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Q-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -2 \\ 2 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-2\cdot (-2) & =0 \\ 4-\lambda -4\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+4 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-5\lambda +8 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the discriminant of the quadratic equation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =(-5)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 8 \\  & =25-32 \\  & =-7 \\  & <0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the characteristic equation does not have real solutions and therefore $Q$ does not have real eigenvalues.
